title: Ezra Collective Secure First U.K. No. 1 Album With ‘Here Because of Hope’
summary: The London-formed jazz band previously peaked at No. 7 in 2024.
contentText:
Ezra Collective has earned its first-ever U.K. No. 1 album with fourth LP Here Because of Hope on the chart published Friday (Sept 18).

The London-formed jazz group lands atop the Official Albums Chart for the first time, following 2019’s You Can’t Steal My Joy (No. 70), 2023’s Where I’m Meant to Be (No. 24) and 2024’s Dance, No One’s Watching (No. 7).

The group has achieved a number of critical highs in recent years. In 2023, they won the Mercury Prize for Where I’m Meant to Be , becoming the first jazz act to take the award; two years later, at the 2025 BRIT Awards, they scored the group of the year trophy.

Speaking to Billboard U.K. , bandleader Femi Koleoso discussed the group’s legacy a decade on from its first release and being cited as an inspiration for rising musicians. “It’s beautiful because people only can aspire to be that if they think it’s accessible and possible, and that’s how I want to come across all the time,” he said.

Michael Jackson ’s The Essential greatest hits collection lifts two spots up to No. 2, while Olivia Rodrigo ’s you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love holds its position at No. 3. Sienna Spiro’s Visitor lifts two spots to No. 4 as her song “Great Expectation” lands a second week at the summit of the Official Singles Chart.

Oasis’ Time Flies: 1994-2009 compilation rockets 10 places up to No. 5 following the announcement of its 2027 world tour . The band confirmed on Monday (Sept. 14) that it would hit the road for 38 shows across the U.K., Ireland, mainland Europe and U.S. next year, kicking off in Glasgow on May 21.

Bloc Party secures a sixth top 10 with Anatomy of a Brief Romance landing at No. 6. Southampton-born musician RØRY scores a first top 10 with Bloodletting at No. 8. Bonobo scores a fourth consecutive top 40 album with Distance in Static at No. 11.
